newsitem.title: JAPAN: Regional power firms to follow TEPCO's price cut.
newsitem.headline: Regional power firms to follow TEPCO's price cut.

text.p: Japan's regional power firms on Friday rushed to express their intention to cut electricity rates after Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc (TEPCO) announced it would cut rates early next year.
Chugoku Electric Power Co Inc, which serves about 7.8 million people in western Japan, said in a statement that it also plans to lower its prices sometime early next year.
Another utility, Shikoku Electric Power Co Inc said it would look promptly into the possibility of cutting prices and said that it may lower rates around the same time.
Shikoku Electric services a total 2.7 million households, shops and factories on Shikoku, the smallest of Japan's four main islands.
None of the firms, including TEPCO, indicated by how much their rates would be cut.
TEPCO's announcement was immediately welcomed by Trade Minister Shinji Sato's who urged other electric power utilities to follow suit.
The Japanese government said last year it aims to bring Japan's electricity prices into line with international levels by 2001 as part of a wider economic reform programme.
It plans to announce detailed measures to carry out the programme later this month.
According to industry estimates, the average Japanese household pays about 20 to 30 percent more for its electricity than counterparts in some Western countries.
